packageRules.description: The third-party action SHAs pinned inside the reusable workflows and composite actions ARE this repo's product: a bump changes what every consumer executes, so it must ship. Labelling it `fix` makes release-please cut a patch for the component whose files changed (release-please attributes by file path -- a bump to actions/generate-sbom releases generate-sbom, a bump inside a reusable workflow releases workflows). Everything the preset already classifies as chore (this repo's own tooling, lock-file maintenance) stays silent.

Undo the rule above for the `_`-prefixed workflows (_release.yml, this repo's OWN release-please runner; _validate.yml, its self-test CI), which no consumer calls -- a bump to an action inside them changes nothing a consumer executes and must not cut a release. They live under .github/workflows/, so without this override their bumps would be attributed to the `workflows` component and release it. The `_` prefix marks a file as ci-internal (vs the bare reusable-workflow filenames). Composes with grouped branches: generateBranchConfig picks the highest-priority type among grouped upgrades (chore < ci < build < fix < feat), so a branch mixing a ci-internal bump with a real reusable-workflow bump still releases as `fix`; only a ci-internal-exclusive bump stays `chore` and silent. Deny-list ci-internal files by prefix rather than allow-list the reusable ones, so a newly added reusable workflow releases by default.

Batch action bumps weekly. Each bump is typed `fix` (rule above) and so cuts a release, and every release opens a pin-bump PR in every consumer; near-daily upstream releases (e.g. claude-code-action) would otherwise cascade a release per day across the fleet. Vulnerability fixes are excluded so the preset's fix(security) rule keeps its `at any time` schedule -- local rules apply after preset rules, so an unscoped schedule here would override it.
